from: From the anguish of his soul he will see and be satisfied[a]; by his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many[b], and he will bear their iniquities.
to: From the anguish of his soul he will see light[a] and be satisfied; by his knowledge[b] my righteous servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities.
rationale: Comparisons of surviving Hebrew source witnesses support adding ‘light’ in Isaiah 53:11; this source choice remains provisional. Published transcriptions of the Dead Sea Scrolls 1QIsaᵃ and 1QIsaᵇ preserve the Hebrew word אור (‘light’), with partial support from 4QIsaᵈ. The Masoretic Text lacks the word; the Greek has ‘to show him light,’ a related reading with different syntax. POB therefore adopts ‘he will see light’ in its selected Hebrew source and English, retaining the shorter alternative and uncertainty in the note. This is evidence from ancient Hebrew source comparisons, not a newly deciphered word or proof that the original wording has been recovered. The word alone does not prove resurrection or identify the servant. The exact source, English and notes were reviewed and the applied book export was verified.
